comparison: Both address the foundational observation of elevated Ca2+ in zyd mutants (C2, C3). OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with converging data from multiple approaches. Peer reviewers also SUPPORT this as the accepted starting point of the study, with Reviewer 1 acknowledging it extends prior work. OpenEval also covers behavioral claims (C28, C29) that peer reviewers request raw data for (R13).

Both evaluate morphological analysis of cortex glia (C20-C23). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED (p>0.05 for all comparisons, including TEM). Peer Reviewer 2 finds this UNCERTAIN, explicitly challenging the low-resolution confocal images and requesting single-cell analysis (MARCM, Brainbow) and better TEM, indicating insufficient evidence quality.

Both address conditional knockdown experiments (C24, C25). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED, confirming cell-type specificity and ruling out developmental effects. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 questioning why RNAi causes lethality when the mutant is viable, and Reviewer 3 suggesting the mutation may be hypomorphic, requesting CRISPR null alleles or conditional rescue instead.

Both evaluate baseline neuronal function claims (C26, C31-C33). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED (p=0.3191 for voltage threshold). Peer Reviewer 1 finds this UNCERTAIN, challenging the definition of 'seizure' criteria and objecting to the interpretation of 'intrinsic excitability' without direct central neuron recordings.

OpenEval R4 addresses baseline neuronal function (C31-C33) as part of broader evaluation, finding evidence SUPPORTED. Peer R14 evaluates overlapping claims (C30-C33) and finds them SUPPORTED without concerns, agreeing these control experiments demonstrate specificity rather than general dysfunction.

Both evaluate cacophony knockdown rescue experiments (C27, C34). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED (p=0.0004), establishing requirement for neuron-glia interaction. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 noting the data without raising concerns about the interpretation.

Both evaluate calcineurin knockdown rescue (C35-C41). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with multiple RNAi lines, alleles, and dose-dependent effects. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 noting that Flybase indicates the RNAi constructs are overlapping (not independent) and have homology to CanB, requesting mutant analysis. Editorial summary emphasizes this as a major concern requiring classical mutations.

Both address CanA subunit knockdowns (C42-C44). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED showing functional redundancy with ~90% rescue for combined knockdown. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY as part of broader calcineurin concerns (R4), requesting mutant analysis for CanA-14F and Pp2B14D instead of relying on RNAi.

Both evaluate Ca2+ imaging showing CN acts downstream of elevated Ca2+ (C45, C46). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED, establishing epistasis. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 requesting primary sample data for calcium transients in Figure 2 and 5, indicating inability to fully evaluate without examining raw imaging data.

Both evaluate CalexA system quantification of CN activity (C47-C50). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with bidirectional changes (p<0.0001). Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 noting that the image in Figure 3 does not match the Western blot and quantification data, indicating a discrepancy that undermines confidence.

Both evaluate pharmacological CN inhibition (C51-C54). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with dose-dependent rescue (~80% at 1mM, p<0.0001), acknowledging possible off-target effects. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 challenging that the cellular specificity (glial vs neuronal) is not established by the data.

Both evaluate sandman knockdown phenocopy (C55-C58). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with cortex glial-specific effects. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN, requesting classical mutations instead of RNAi. Reviewer 1 notes both mutants are fully penetrant, making epistasis analysis inconclusive, and suggests testing double heterozygotes or overexpression in zyd background.

Both evaluate epistasis between sand and CN (C59, C60). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED, placing sand downstream of CN. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN as part of broader sandman concerns (R8), with the editorial summary noting reliance on RNAi and requesting classical mutations despite prior publications using RNAi.

Both evaluate SAND phosphorylation status (C61-C63). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED that phosphorylation is unchanged, arguing against direct CN-mediated dephosphorylation. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 noting that negative kinase inhibitor results don't allow conclusions and requesting specific sandman mutants.

Both evaluate SAND:GFP membrane localization (C64-C66). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED showing specific reduction in zyd cortex glia. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 identifying the key missing experiment: directly testing whether Sand is abnormally endocytosed in zyd mutants by examining surface vs. endosomal distribution.

Both evaluate endocytosis disruption rescue (C67-C69). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with chronic knockdown providing complete rescue. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 calling this 'the weakest point of the data set' and suggesting removal, while Reviewer 2 questions whether the data show enhanced endocytosis versus cell swelling.

Both evaluate Rab5::GFP early endosome imaging (C70, C71). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED (p=0.0088 for zyd increase, p=0.0378 for CsA normalization). Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 noting Rab5 examination could indicate many different changes, and Reviewer 2 stating the image suggests swollen cells rather than enhanced endocytosis, requesting endogenous Rab5 labeling.

Both evaluate Shibire temperature-sensitive experiments (C72, C73). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED, arguing for chronic rather than acute endocytic effects. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN as part of broader endocytosis concerns (R10), with the editorial summary noting differences in opinion about necessity of endocytosis data given difficulty creating reagents to directly follow K+ channel trafficking.

Both evaluate K+ conductance rescue experiments (C74-C78). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with partial to substantial rescue (~60-75%). Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 questioning whether EKO overexpression specifically reverses the phenotype or non-specifically clamps cells at K+ equilibrium, and Reviewer 2 asking whether Na+ increase would produce similar suppression, questioning specificity of K+ buffering interpretation.

Both evaluate the overall mechanistic model (C4, C5, C7, C8, C79). OpenEval finds the linear pathway model SUPPORTED by epistasis, pharmacology, and functional rescue, noting some connections rely on inference. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 noting the missing experiment showing Sand is abnormally endocytosed in zyd, and Reviewer 1 noting the weak connection to channel trafficking. Editorial summary concludes the paper could be exceptional but requires additional work beyond eLife policy timeframe.

OpenEval evaluates background literature on astrocyte-neuron communication and glial Ca2+ in epilepsy (C9-C16), finding citations SUPPORTED though noting debate about cultured cell study relevance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

Both evaluate anatomical organization of Drosophila glia (C1, C17-C19). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 praising the novel emphasis on glia restricted to soma/initial processes. However, Reviewer 2 raises a conceptual question about functional interpretation given unipolar insect neurons, though not challenging the anatomical claims themselves.

OpenEval evaluates background on epilepsy prevalence and translational relevance (C80-C83), finding claims SUPPORTED though noting C82 lacks specific citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates background literature on TRESK/sandman regulation (C84, C85), finding citations SUPPORTED and noting importance for interpreting phosphorylation results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates literature on glial K+ channels (C86-C89), finding citations SUPPORTED and noting justification for investigating alternative channels. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates speculative claim about general CN regulation mechanism (C90), finding it UNCERTAIN as it extends beyond presented data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this relates to the broader mechanistic model concerns in peer R17.

OpenEval R1 includes behavioral/Ca2+ imaging claims (C28, C29) as part of broader evaluation finding evidence SUPPORTED. Peer R13 specifically requests primary sample data for calcium transients, finding these claims UNCERTAIN without ability to examine raw imaging data.
